Ui.Script:
BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS = 4
-- The 1.12 item-quality palette — now the shared ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS global (Fonts.xml, -- its home since the unit popup became a second customer); the local name kept for this -- file's existing readers. Indexed 0..6; an unknown/nil quality falls back to common. BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS = ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS
local function loot_color(quality) return BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS[quality] or BENILLA_LOOT_QUALITY_COLORS[1] end
-- ── Master loot (decision 1675) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The quality at or above which handing an item out asks for confirmation first. Ref -- LootFrame.lua l.3 — and the misspelling is Blizzard's own, kept because the corpus -- reads THIS name: `MASTER_LOOT_THRESHOLD` (with the S) exists nowhere in 1.12. MASTER_LOOT_THREHOLD = 4
GIVE_LOOT = GIVE_LOOT or "Give Loot To:" -- l.2006 GROUP = GROUP or "Group" -- l.2029 -- The party bound the dropdown's party arm sweeps to (ref PartyMemberFrame.lua l.1; ours -- is declared in PartyFrame.xml, which the manifest loads far ahead of this file). Stated -- through the same first-writer-wins idiom as the strings above rather than assumed: the -- dropdown's init function RUNS at this file's load (UIDropDownMenu_Initialize calls it -- immediately), so a missing constant is an arithmetic error at load, not at first use. MAX_PARTY_MEMBERS = MAX_PARTY_MEMBERS or 4 -- The raid arm's two bounds, same idiom and same reason (declared in PartyFrame.xml / -- RaidFrame.xml, both loaded first). The reference writes them inline as literal `40` and -- `5` (l.194/:195); naming them is ours, so the names have to be guaranteed here. MAX_RAID_MEMBERS = MAX_RAID_MEMBERS or 40 MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP = MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP or 5 CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION = CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION or "You wish to assign %s to %s. Is this correct?" -- l.848 -- The dialog below captures these two by VALUE at load, so a load-order slip would bake a -- nil into its buttons rather than fail loudly. FriendsFrame.xml declares them and the -- manifest loads it first; stated again here so this file's own dialog cannot depend on -- that staying true. YES = YES or "Yes" -- l.5463 NO = NO or "No" -- l.2794
-- The confirmation the dropdown raises for an at-or-above-threshold item (ref -- StaticPopup.lua l.85-94). `data` is the candidate index the dropdown stashed; the SLOT -- is re-read live from LootFrame.selectedSlot at accept time, exactly as the ref does — -- which is precisely why the row click below hides this popup first, so an accept can -- never land on a row the player has since clicked away from. StaticPopupDialogs["CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION"] = { text = CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION, button1 = YES, button2 = NO, OnAccept = function(data) GiveMasterLoot(LootFrame.selectedSlot, data) end, timeout = 0, hideOnEscape = 1, }
function BenillaLootItem_OnLoad(button, index) button.lootButton = index button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.name = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Name") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") -- Left-click loots the row (the C LootButton behaviour, LootFrame.lua l.94/147). button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") end
-- ref LootFrameItem_OnClick (LootFrame.lua l.147-162): CTRL previews the row's item in the -- dressing room (decision 1060), SHIFT posts its link into an open chat edit box (decision -- 1059) — both through GetLootSlotLink, the row-link binding this arc added (loot.rs). -- -- WHERE THE TAKE LIVES, and why the gate below reads three modifiers where FrameXML names -- two (VERIFIED at the 1.12.1 bytes — wow-re `ui/scratch/loot-click-modifier-gate.md`, -- decision 1067). The reference's Lua handler suppresses NOTHING, because the take is the C -- `CLootButton`'s own click behaviour (`LootFrame.lua:94`'s `button:SetSlot(slot)` hands the -- widget the slot). `CLootButton::OnClick 0x4c1820` runs the Lua `<OnClick>` FIRST and -- unconditionally, then gates itself on `0x41f8f0(0/1/2)` — byte-identically the predicates -- behind `IsShiftKeyDown`/`IsControlKeyDown`/**`IsAltKeyDown`** — and only then sends -- (`0x4c2790` → `0x5e1ad0` → `push 0x108`, CMSG_AUTOSTORE_LOOT_ITEM). -- -- Three consequences, all of them this handler's shape: -- · **ALT suppresses the take too**, though no FrameXML file mentions alt. Its gate is C. -- · The gate is on ANY modifier being HELD, not on "the arm that handled it": a shift-click -- with the chat box closed does nothing in Lua and still must not loot. -- · The button code is never read (`0x4c1820` doesn't look at it), so a RIGHT-click loots -- exactly like a left one — which is why this handler takes no `mouseButton`. -- -- benilla folds that C action into this Lua handler, so the gate has to be an early return -- here. The verb it calls is `BenillaTakeLootSlot`, not `LootSlot`, and that is 1067's -- named follow-up landed (decision 1744): 1.12 exposes no plain "take slot N" binding at -- all — the real `LootSlot 0x4c2e70` is the LOOT_BIND *confirmation continuation* (flag 1, -- gated on the stashed slot at `[0x847cec]`; its only FrameXML caller is -- `StaticPopup.lua:606`, the entry below). Ours keeps exactly that meaning, so an addon -- calling `LootSlot(n)` on an ordinary row does what it does on the real client: nothing. -- -- The reference's tail (StaticPopup_Hide("CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION") and the four -- LootFrame.selected* fields, l.155-161) is the MASTER-LOOT dropdown's bookkeeping — -- GroupLootDropDown reads exactly those four (l.164+). benilla ships no master loot -- (benilla-protocol's loot module: CMSG_LOOT_MASTER_GIVE/SMSG_LOOT_MASTER_LIST out of -- scope), so returning early skips nothing that exists. -- -- The coin row has no link (it is synthesized, with no item behind it — ui_loot.rs), so a -- modified click on it finds nil: DressUpItemLink returns on a nil link (DressUpFrame.lua -- l.10-16) and the insert is skipped. It does not fall through to looting the money either, -- which is the same law the item rows follow. function BenillaLootItem_OnClick(button) -- The row remembers its resolved loot slot from the last Update; act on it (LootFrame.lua -- l.94-95 stores button.slot, the click calls LootSlot on it). if not button.slot then return end local modified = false if IsControlKeyDown() then DressUpItemLink(GetLootSlotLink(button.slot)) -- ref l.148-149 modified = true elseif IsShiftKeyDown() then -- ref l.150-153, through the shared helper (UIParent.xml): it carries the ref's own -- "only when the edit box is up" guard AND our nil-link one, which this row needs -- more than most — the coin row never has a link, and an item row has none until -- its template lands. A shift-click with chat closed does nothing here: a loot row -- has no stack to split, unlike a bag slot. BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetLootSlotLink(button.slot)) modified = true elseif IsAltKeyDown() then -- The C gate's third modifier (`0x41f8f0(2)` @ `0x4c1841`). Nothing is bound to -- alt in FrameXML, so this arm does nothing at all — its entire job is to NOT -- loot, which is what the real client does and what we did not. modified = true end
-- The ref's tail (l.155-161), and it runs on EVERY click — modified ones included, -- because in the reference this bookkeeping is the Lua <OnClick> and the take is the -- C handler that runs after it; the modifier gate lives in the C half, so it never -- skipped these four. Ours folds the take into this function (1067), so the tail is -- lifted above the early return rather than left below it — same observable. -- -- What reads them: GroupLootDropDown, which the app opens by firing -- OPEN_MASTER_LOOT_LIST when the clicked row's wire slot_type is MASTER. That event -- is raised from the pick drain, i.e. AFTER this handler returns, so the four fields -- must already be stashed by then — they are the dropdown's only knowledge of WHICH -- row is being handed out, and its anchor. StaticPopup_Hide("CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION") LootFrame.selectedLootButton = button:GetName() LootFrame.selectedSlot = button.slot LootFrame.selectedQuality = button.quality LootFrame.selectedItemName = button.name:GetText()
if modified then return end BenillaTakeLootSlot(button.slot) end
-- Hover: the plain engine item tooltip, ITEM rows only — the ref's own gate (its -- LootButtonTemplate <OnEnter> runs SetLootItem only `if LootSlotIsItem(slot)`, so the -- coin pile shows no tooltip at all). No hand-added lines: the real tooltip never shows a -- stack size (the 0274 P1 'Stack Size' drop retired the same line from the bag hovers; -- this file's copy predated it and survived). function BenillaLootItem_OnEnter(button) if not button.slot then return end if not LootSlotIsItem(button.slot) then return end local texture, item, quantity, quality, itemId = GetLootSlotInfo(button.slot) button.itemId = itemId if not item then return end -- Snap beside the ICON, not the 160-wide row's far edge (the vendor rows' own idiom — -- MerchantFrame.xml walks ANCHOR_RIGHT back by a negative x): 37px icon on a 160 row -- → -123 lands the tip at the icon's right edge. GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT", -123, 0) -- SetLootItem, like the ref's own LootButtonTemplate: the loot ROW is the source, not -- just its item id, so the tooltip sees the drop's random-suffix roll. Through -- SetItemById (a template source) a "… of the Monkey" showed `<Random enchantment>` -- until the item reached a bag — decision 1547. GameTooltip:SetLootItem(button.slot) GameTooltip:Show() end
function BenillaLootItem_OnLeave(button) GameTooltip:Hide() end
-- LootFrame_Update (LootFrame.lua l.67-119): fill the visible rows for the current page. function LootFrame_Update() local frame = getglobal("LootFrame") local numItems = GetNumLootItems() -- Rows per page: 4, or 3 when there's a pager to make room for (l.70-73). local perPage = BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS if numItems > BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS then perPage = perPage - 1 end -- Clamp the page. numItems is constant while a window is open (cleared slots stay in -- the count — the fixed slot layout), so this only guards a stray page value. local maxPage = 1 if numItems > 0 then maxPage = math.ceil(numItems / perPage) end if frame.page > maxPage then frame.page = maxPage end if frame.page < 1 then frame.page = 1 end
for index = 1, BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS do local button = getglobal("LootButton" .. index) local slot = (perPage * (frame.page - 1)) + index if slot <= numItems and index <= perPage and (LootSlotIsItem(slot) or LootSlotIsCoin(slot)) then local texture, item, quantity, quality, itemId = GetLootSlotInfo(slot) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) button.name:SetText(item or "...") local color = loot_color(quality) button.name:SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) -- "xN" stack count only when more than one drops (LootFrame.lua l.87-93). if (quantity or 1) > 1 then button.count:SetText(quantity) else button.count:SetText("") end button.slot = slot button.itemId = itemId -- Ref l.96. Read back by the row click into LootFrame.selectedQuality, which -- is what decides whether handing this row out asks for confirmation first. button.quality = quality button:Show() else button:Hide() end end
-- Pager visibility (LootFrame.lua l.105-118): Up when past page 1, Down when more remain. if frame.page > 1 then getglobal("LootUpButton"):Show() else getglobal("LootUpButton"):Hide() end if frame.page < maxPage then getglobal("LootDownButton"):Show() else getglobal("LootDownButton"):Hide() end end
function LootFrame_PageDown() local frame = getglobal("LootFrame") frame.page = frame.page + 1 LootFrame_Update() end
function LootFrame_PageUp() local frame = getglobal("LootFrame") frame.page = frame.page - 1 LootFrame_Update() end
-- ── The soulbind confirm ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- ref GlobalStrings.lua l.2612 / l.2818 / l.465, fallback form (the player's own localized -- file runs off the patch chain first). LOOT_NO_DROP = LOOT_NO_DROP or "Looting this item will bind it to you." OKAY = OKAY or "Okay" CANCEL = CANCEL or "Cancel"
-- ref StaticPopup.lua l.601-611, verbatim. `OnAccept`'s argument is `dialog.data`, which -- the driver below sets to the event's row — and `LootSlot` is the continuation verb, so -- this line is the ONLY thing in the client that ever completes a bind-deferred take. -- -- Nothing else is needed: no OnCancel (declining just leaves the row in the window, and the -- app drops the pending stash when the window turns over) and no OnUpdate poll, because the -- window's own LOOT_CLOSED hides it (below, ref LootFrame.lua l.53-54). StaticPopupDialogs["LOOT_BIND"] = { text = LOOT_NO_DROP, button1 = OKAY, button2 = CANCEL, OnAccept = function(slot) LootSlot(slot) end, timeout = 0, exclusive = 1, hideOnEscape = 1, }
-- ref UIParent.lua l.317-323. The row rides on `dialog.data` rather than as a text arg — -- LOOT_NO_DROP has no format specifier, so the dialog shows the same sentence whatever -- binds; the number is only there to be handed back to LootSlot. -- -- The reference registers this on UIParent, which owns every bind confirm; benilla hangs it -- on LootFrame, whose LOOT_CLOSED already has to hide the dialog. Same two moments, one -- listener, and the arc stays in one file. function BenillaLootBindConfirm(slot) local dialog = StaticPopup_Show("LOOT_BIND") if dialog then dialog.data = slot end end
function LootFrame_OnLoad() local frame = this frame.page = 1 frame:RegisterEvent("LOOT_OPENED") frame:RegisterEvent("LOOT_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("LOOT_CLOSED") frame:RegisterEvent("LOOT_BIND_CONFIRM") -- Master loot (ref l.9-10). Neither event carries an argument: the candidate list is -- read back through GetMasterLootCandidate at menu-build time, not pushed. frame:RegisterEvent("OPEN_MASTER_LOOT_LIST") frame:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_MASTER_LOOT_LIST") end
function LootFrame_OnEvent(event) local frame = this if event == "LOOT_OPENED" then -- A fresh loot: reset to page 1, paint, show (LootFrame.lua l.14-16). frame.page = 1 LootFrame_Update() ShowUIPanel(frame) elseif event == "LOOT_UPDATE" then -- A content change while open (name/quality landed, a row/coin removed): repaint, -- keeping the current page. A looted slot's button hides IN PLACE (the slot stays -- in the layout as a gap — the ref's LOOT_SLOT_CLEARED, l.22-37). LootFrame_Update() -- The ref's LOOT_SLOT_CLEARED tail (l.38-50): a page left with every button hidden -- moves down to the next page when one exists. local allHidden = true for index = 1, BENILLA_LOOT_NUMBUTTONS do if getglobal("LootButton" .. index):IsVisible() then allHidden = false end end if allHidden and getglobal("LootDownButton"):IsVisible() then LootFrame_PageDown() end elseif event == "LOOT_CLOSED" then -- ref l.53-54: the confirm dies with the window it addressed. Its row number would -- name a slot in the NEXT corpse otherwise. StaticPopup_Hide("LOOT_BIND") HideUIPanel(frame) elseif event == "LOOT_BIND_CONFIRM" then BenillaLootBindConfirm(arg1) elseif event == "OPEN_MASTER_LOOT_LIST" then -- Ref l.58-61. Anchored to the ROW that was clicked, not to the frame — the name -- the click stashed a moment ago. ToggleDropDownMenu(1, nil, GroupLootDropDown, LootFrame.selectedLootButton, 0, 0) elseif event == "UPDATE_MASTER_LOOT_LIST" then -- Ref l.62-64: refresh IN PLACE, never re-toggle — re-toggling an open menu would -- close it under the player's cursor. UIDropDownMenu_Refresh(GroupLootDropDown) end end
function LootFrame_OnShow() -- Open sound — the window-sound convention (decision 0090), wrapper form (this handler -- has real logic beyond the sound, so it can't be a bare inline PlaySound). -- (LootFrame.lua LootFrame_OnShow, l.131-141). ONLY the empty-roll fork and the fishing -- fork are Lua-side: an empty loot plays LOOTWINDOWOPENEMPTY (l.135-136); a fishing loot -- (IsFishingLoot(), decision 1086) plays "FISHING REEL IN" and swaps the portrait ring's -- skull for the FishingLoot-Icon (l.137-140) — reset to the skull first, exactly as the -- ref does (l.133), so a corpse loot after a fishing one gets its skull back. The normal -- (non-empty, non-fishing) loot-open sound is C-side (the server-driven loot handler), -- so we stay silent for it — there is no kit to guess. (DR 0086: vmangos masks the -- lootable flag for empty rolls, so a live empty window is rare — but the branch must -- exist.) getglobal("LootPortraitOverlay"):SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\TargetDead") if GetNumLootItems() == 0 then PlaySound("LOOTWINDOWOPENEMPTY") elseif IsFishingLoot() then PlaySound("FISHING REEL IN") getglobal("LootPortraitOverlay"):SetTexture("Interface\\LootFrame\\FishingLoot-Icon") end end
function LootFrame_OnHide() -- Closing the window releases the loot (LootFrame.lua l.143-145). The app only sends the -- release when a loot is actually open, so a hide after the state already cleared is a -- harmless no-op. No close sound here: LootFrame_OnHide plays none (the loot-close kit is -- C-side), so we stay silent — no kit to guess. CloseLoot() end
function BenillaLootCloseButton_OnClick() -- Hide immediately (client-authoritative); OnHide's CloseLoot() sends the release. HideUIPanel(getglobal("LootFrame")) end
-- ── GroupLootDropDown — the master looter's "Give Loot To:" menu ────────────────────── -- Ref LootFrame.lua l.164-244, transcribed. The frame keeps the reference's BARE name for -- the same mechanical reason the four GroupLootFrames do (decision 1254/0591 §3): -- LootFrame_OnEvent resolves it by literal global lookup, and a real 1.12 addon that -- hooks the master-loot menu expects to find it under this name.
function GroupLootDropDown_OnLoad() -- "MENU" style: a bare context menu, no capsule chrome — it is opened at the loot row -- by ToggleDropDownMenu, never drawn in place. Passed by name rather than the ref's -- bare `this`, the house calling convention (TradeSkillFrame/TrainerFrame precedent). UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(GroupLootDropDown, GroupLootDropDown_Initialize, "MENU") end
function GroupLootDropDown_Initialize() local candidate, info
-- Level 2: one raid group's five candidate slots (ref l.170-184). The parent row -- stashed the index its probe found, and this walks the five starting THERE — so a -- group whose first present candidate is not its first slot yields a window offset by -- the same amount. That is the reference's own arithmetic; kept as-is. if UIDROPDOWNMENU_MENU_LEVEL == 2 then local lastIndex = UIDROPDOWNMENU_MENU_VALUE + 5 - 1 for i = UIDROPDOWNMENU_MENU_VALUE, lastIndex do candidate = GetMasterLootCandidate(i) if candidate then info = {} info.text = candidate info.textHeight = 12 info.value = i info.notCheckable = 1 info.func = GroupLootDropDown_GiveLoot UIDropDownMenu_AddButton(info, UIDROPDOWNMENU_MENU_LEVEL) end end return end
if GetNumRaidMembers() > 0 then -- In a raid: a title, then one nested row per group that has any candidate at all -- (ref l.186-212). The probe is "does any of this block of five answer non-nil". info = {} info.text = GIVE_LOOT info.textHeight = 12 info.notCheckable = 1 info.isTitle = 1 UIDropDownMenu_AddButton(info) for i = 1, MAX_RAID_MEMBERS, MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP do for j = i, i + MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP - 1 do candidate = GetMasterLootCandidate(j) if candidate then info = {} -- The label counts from the loop step `i`, the value from the found -- slot `j` — the ref uses the two differently on purpose (l.196/:200). info.text = GROUP .. " " .. math.ceil(i / MEMBERS_PER_RAID_GROUP) info.textHeight = 12 info.hasArrow = 1 info.notCheckable = 1 info.value = j info.func = nil UIDropDownMenu_AddButton(info) break end end end else -- In a party: a flat list, no title row and no nesting (ref l.214-232). The sweep -- is MAX_PARTY_MEMBERS+1 because the master looter can hand loot to THEMSELVES — -- the server includes us in the candidate list too (Group::MasterLoot walks the -- whole group). for i = 1, MAX_PARTY_MEMBERS + 1, 1 do candidate = GetMasterLootCandidate(i) if candidate then info = {} info.text = candidate info.textHeight = 12 info.value = i info.notCheckable = 1 info.func = GroupLootDropDown_GiveLoot UIDropDownMenu_AddButton(info) end end end end
function GroupLootDropDown_GiveLoot() -- Ref l.234-244. At or above the threshold the assignment is confirmed first; below -- it, it goes straight out. The popup's message takes the quality-coloured item name -- and the candidate's own row text. -- -- The `selectedQuality and` guard is ours, and it is required rather than defensive: -- benilla resolves an item template asynchronously, so GetLootSlotInfo answers a nil -- quality (and a nil name) for a row whose template is still in flight — a state the -- real client's C-side loot record never has. Unguarded, that comparison raises. A nil -- quality takes the below-threshold arm, which is the safe direction: the assignment -- still happens, it just doesn't ask first. if LootFrame.selectedQuality and LootFrame.selectedQuality >= MASTER_LOOT_THREHOLD then local color = ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS[LootFrame.selectedQuality] local dialog = StaticPopup_Show("CONFIRM_LOOT_DISTRIBUTION", color.hex .. (LootFrame.selectedItemName or "") .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE, this:GetText()) if dialog then dialog.data = this.value end else GiveMasterLoot(LootFrame.selectedSlot, this.value) end CloseDropDownMenus() end
